cues.text: Percent complete is cost so far over expected total cost. Every job recomputes.
A change order adds to a contract's price. One was booked $370,000 higher than the owner signed.
It tests each job's cost estimate against later bills. One job's costs jumped about $1.2 million, but only after year end.
Last, it weighs the findings against materiality, the size of mistake that matters, and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. Known mistakes add up to $103,600 of revenue from that change order, under materiality. Bigger judgment calls go to the CPA: the $1.2 million cost jump and about $407,000 of shrinking profit on another job. Eight items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
